Hello,

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry about the trouble with your payment. I understand a failed-payment notice is stressful, especially after your finance team has already updated the card. Here are the steps to resolve it and an answer on your data.

**Why the payment may have failed (ACCT-001)**
This error means we couldn't process your recurring subscription payment. Common causes are:
- The card was declined by the issuing bank, or flagged for fraud
- Insufficient funds or an expired card
- A temporary payment provider issue

Updating the card doesn't always trigger a new charge on its own. You may also need to retry the payment manually.

**Steps to resolve**
1. Log in to the CloudSync Dashboard and go to **Account > Billing**.
2. Check that the new card appears under your payment method. Confirm the card number, expiration date, CVV, and billing zip code are correct. If anything is wrong, click **Update Payment Method** and re-enter the details.
3. Click **Retry Payment**.
4. If the payment is declined again, please ask your finance team to contact the card's issuing bank. Banks sometimes block recurring online charges or flag them as suspicious, and they can approve the charge or tell you why it was declined.
5. Let us know the result, and we'll verify on our side that the payment went through.

**What happens to your data if the payment isn't resolved**
- **Grace period:** After a failed payment you have a **7-day grace period**. Your account keeps working normally during this time.
- **After the grace period:** If the payment is still unresolved, the account is downgraded to the **Free plan**. Your files are **not deleted** by a downgrade. However, the Free plan includes 5 GB of storage, 3 devices, and 1 user. If your usage exceeds those limits, **syncing will pause** until the payment is resolved or usage is reduced. Some Pro features, such as Team Spaces, would also become unavailable.
- **Prolonged non-payment:** If an account stays overdue for a longer period, it can be suspended and all sync operations paused. Data is preserved for 30 days after suspension, and you can restore access by updating your payment method and paying the outstanding balance.

Because the grace period is time-sensitive, I recommend retrying the payment as soon as possible. If you can tell me roughly when the failure notice arrived, I can confirm exactly how many days of the grace period remain.

If the retry fails or you'd like us to look at your billing status, reply here and we'll help right away. Please don't send full card numbers by email. Just tell us the last four digits and the error message you see, if any.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

Hi there,

The ACCT-002 (Plan Limit Reached) error means an action would go over a limit on your current plan. The Pro plan includes up to 25 team members. If your team has 25 people, your workspace is at that maximum. The invite button is greyed out because adding a 26th member would exceed the limit.

Here's how to check and fix it:

1. **Check your usage.** Go to Dashboard > Account > Usage and look at the team member count. Please also confirm your plan under Dashboard > Account > Plans.
2. **Free up seats if you can.** If anyone on the list has left the company or no longer needs access, removing them should free a seat so you can invite someone new. Please also look for any accounts you didn't expect to see in the count.
3. **Upgrade if you need more than 25 members.** The Enterprise plan has unlimited team members, storage and devices. Enterprise is custom-priced, with a minimum commitment of 50 seats on annual billing. For a quote, go to Dashboard > Account > Plans > "Contact Sales" or email sales@cloudsync.io.

If Usage shows fewer than 25 members and you still see this error, please reply with a screenshot of the Usage page and the greyed-out invite button. We'll look into it from our side.

Tell us how many additional people you're planning to add, and we can help work out the best option for your team.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

ACCT-003 (Account Suspended) means the account has been suspended and all sync activity is paused. Your data is not deleted. It is preserved for 30 days from the suspension date.

Suspensions can happen for a few reasons, and the fix depends on which one applies:
- Payment: an overdue balance that has gone past the grace period
- Terms of Service or security: a compliance issue or unusual activity flagged by our security system
- Admin action (Enterprise): a workspace administrator suspended the account

Here is what you can do right now:
1. Open the login page and look for the suspension reason shown with the ACCT-003 message. Please tell us what it says.
2. Check the inbox (and spam folder) of your account owner and billing contact for any email from CloudSync about billing or account status.
3. If the reason is a payment issue, the account owner can go to Dashboard > Account > Billing, choose "Update Payment Method", and pay the outstanding balance. If you can't reach the Dashboard, reply here and we'll help you complete payment another way.
4. If your organization is on an Enterprise plan, check with your internal workspace administrators to confirm that nobody suspended the account on purpose.

On our side, we are reviewing your account's suspension status and history to confirm the exact cause and when it happened. To speed this up, please reply with:
- Your account or workspace name and the email address of the account owner
- The suspension reason shown on the login page, if any
- Your plan type (Pro or Enterprise)
- Whether any recent changes were made, such as a billing update, a new card, or a large number of added users

Once we confirm the cause, we'll tell you exactly what is needed to reactivate the account and will work to get you back in as quickly as we can.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

Hello,

Thank you for reporting this right away. Logins from countries where you have no staff, together with unexpected file downloads, need to be treated as a possible account compromise. We're treating your case as a top-priority security incident.

**Is this a data breach?**
We can't say yet. Unfamiliar logins and downloads are a serious warning sign. But whether data was actually accessed by an unauthorized party depends on what the logs show. For example, the logins could come from a VPN, a traveling employee, or an integration. Reviewing the audit log will tell us. In the meantime, we recommend acting as though it is a real incident.

**What to do right now (workspace Owner/Admin):**

1. **Revoke suspicious sessions.** Go to Admin > Security > Active Sessions. Select any session you don't recognize and click Revoke. If you can't tell which are legitimate, use "Revoke All" to sign everyone out. Users will need to log in again.
2. **Reset credentials.** Have the affected users, and ideally all admins, change their passwords. If you use SSO, also reset or terminate sessions and reset credentials for those users in your identity provider (Okta, Azure AD, etc.). Note that the workspace Owner can always log in with email and password, so make sure the Owner password is changed and secure.
3. **Check 2FA.** Confirm that two-factor authentication is enabled on all accounts, especially admins. Go to Account Settings > Security.
4. **Review the Audit Log.** Go to Admin > Audit Log and filter by the date range of last night. Look at login events, file downloads and shares, user or role changes, and API key creation. You can export the results as a CSV to keep as a record.
5. **Check for other access routes.** Go to Admin > API Keys and revoke any keys you don't recognize or that were created recently. Also review Admin > Settings history for changes you didn't make, and check that no unfamiliar users or role changes have appeared.
6. **Preserve evidence.** Don't delete logs, accounts or files. Please also save any alerts from your own security tools (SIEM or SOAR) that flagged this activity.

**To help us investigate, please reply with:**
- The approximate timestamps and countries of the suspicious logins
- The affected user accounts, and whether any of them are admins or Owners
- The files or folders that were downloaded, and how sensitive they are
- Whether SSO and 2FA are enabled on these accounts
- Whether any API keys, integrations or SIEM alerts are involved
- Which of your users, if any, legitimately travel or work abroad

We're also sharing your case with our security team so they can review activity on our side. If the audit log confirms unauthorized access to sensitive data, you may have legal or contractual notification obligations, for example under GDPR or HIPAA. We recommend involving your internal security and legal teams now. We can give them the logs and information they need.

We'll stay engaged until this is resolved. Please reply as soon as you've completed the first steps, or sooner if you see any new unfamiliar activity or have trouble with any step.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry about the disruption. I understand that orders are backing up while webhook deliveries to https://api.bigretail.com/hooks/cloudsync are failing. We're treating this as urgent.

What the error means
API-002 (Webhook Delivery Failed) means CloudSync couldn't complete delivery to your endpoint. A "Connection timed out" on every attempt usually means our delivery requests aren't reaching your server, or your server isn't responding within our 10-second window. This can happen even when nothing was deliberately changed. Common causes are a firewall, WAF or CDN rule update, a load balancer or proxy problem, an expired SSL certificate, or an overloaded application.

Things to check right now (fastest first)
1. Test the endpoint from outside your network. Send a test POST to https://api.bigretail.com/hooks/cloudsync from a public IP, for example from a cloud host or mobile hotspot rather than your office network. It should return a 200 OK in under 10 seconds.
2. Check your load balancer, reverse proxy, WAF or CDN. Look at health checks, recent auto-scaling or deployment events, and any rate-limiting or bot-protection rules that might be blocking or dropping CloudSync's requests. Please also check whether your hosting or network provider made any changes in the last hour or so.
3. Confirm CloudSync's IP ranges are allowed through your firewall. You can find the current ranges in our documentation. Please check that no rule changes or automatic IP-reputation blocks have affected them.
4. Verify your SSL/TLS certificate. Make sure it is valid, unexpired, issued by a trusted CA, and has a complete certificate chain.
5. Check your application's response time. If your handler does heavy processing before responding, acknowledge the request with a 200 right away and process the order asynchronously. Our requests time out after 10 seconds.
6. Send a test event from CloudSync. Go to Dashboard > Settings > Webhooks > Test to trigger a delivery on demand. Once you've made a fix, this confirms quickly whether it worked.

If the test still fails, please check Dashboard > Settings > Webhooks > Delivery Logs and send us the timestamp of the most recent failed attempt. If you can, also send your server or load balancer access logs for the same time. This will help us see whether the requests are reaching you at all.

About the missed events
CloudSync retries each failed webhook 3 times with exponential backoff (after 1s, 10s and 100s). Events that failed during this window may not be redelivered automatically once those retries are used up. I'm checking with our engineering team on the best way to recover the events that were missed, and I'll update you as soon as I have an answer. If anything in your setup did change, such as a deployment, DNS update, certificate renewal or firewall change, let us know and we can narrow this down quickly. Once you've gone through the steps above, reply with what you find and we'll continue from there.

Hi there,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry your nightly export is failing. A 429 with API-001 (Rate Limit Exceeded) means the API rejected requests because your account went over its per-minute limit. Here are the limits and some ways to handle them.

**Your rate limits**

| Plan | Requests/min | Burst (10-second window) |
|------|-------------|--------------------------|
| Free | 100 | 20 |
| Pro | 1,000 | 200 |
| Enterprise | 10,000 (default) | 2,000 |

At about 3,000 requests per minute, your export is well over the Free and Pro limits. It is within the default Enterprise limit. On Enterprise, you could still hit 429s if the script sends more than 2,000 requests in any 10-second window. That can happen even when the per-minute average looks fine.

**How to fix it**

1. **Check your current limit.** Every API response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` headers. You can also call `GET /api/v1/rate-limit-status`. This shows which limit your key is actually subject to.

2. **Add exponential backoff and respect `retry_after`.** A 429 response includes a `retry_after` value in seconds. Wait at least that long before retrying. If it's absent, back off at 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, up to a 60s maximum. Add 0–1s of random jitter, and stop after 5 retries.

3. **Spread requests evenly.** Don't send them in bursts. Watch `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and slow down when it drops below about 20%. Spreading the load usually works better than sending everything as fast as possible. A job that averages 3,000/min can still trip the burst limit.

4. **Cut the number of calls.**
   - For list or metadata calls, use cursor-based pagination with `limit=200`, the maximum. The default is 50, so this alone can cut those calls by up to 4x.
   - Cache file metadata on the client side. It changes infrequently, so there's no need to re-fetch it on every run.
   - If any part of the script polls for changes, use webhooks instead.
   - Our batch endpoints (for example `batch-move` and `batch-delete`) count as a single API call for up to 100 operations. They only cover move, delete, share and invite operations, so they may not apply to the read side of an export.

5. **Choose the right plan.** On Free or Pro, the export will need to run at or below your plan's limit. You can stretch it over a longer window, or upgrade to a higher plan. Enterprise customers can also ask us for a custom rate limit increase.

**To help us narrow this down, could you send us:**
- Your current plan, or your account or organization ID
- Which endpoint(s) the export calls, and roughly how many requests go to each
- A sample 429 response, with auth headers redacted, including the `retry_after` value

**Steps to check**

1. **Confirm the error details in your delivery logs.** Go to Dashboard > Settings > Webhooks > Delivery Logs and look at the failure message for recent attempts. If it mentions a certificate or SSL/TLS problem, that confirms the cause.

2. **Check that the full certificate chain is installed.** A common problem after renewal is that the server presents only the new leaf certificate and not the intermediate certificate(s). Browsers sometimes tolerate this, but automated clients like our webhook service often don't. Make sure your server is configured with the full chain bundle from your certificate authority. You can check what your server presents with:
   `openssl s_client -connect your-endpoint-domain:443 -servername your-endpoint-domain`
   Or use an online SSL checker such as SSL Labs.

3. **Verify the certificate matches your endpoint hostname exactly.** The certificate's CN/SAN must cover the exact domain in your webhook URL. For example, a certificate for `example.com` won't cover `api.example.com` unless it's a wildcard or lists that name.

Hello,

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry your contractor has lost access to the project files. This is disruptive, especially mid-project.

No, this isn't expected. In CloudSync, the Viewer role gives read-only access. A Viewer can open and view files and download them, but can't edit, delete, or share. Moving someone from Editor to Viewer should only remove those editing rights. It shouldn't stop her opening files. There are a few likely explanations, and you can check most of them yourself:

1. Confirm the role and the share. In the workspace admin panel, check that her role now shows as Viewer, and not removed or something else. Then open the shared project folder's Share settings and confirm her account is still listed. Changing a role can sometimes be done by removing and re-adding someone, which would revoke the share.

2. Check whether she was set to "Restricted Viewer". This is a separate permission level. It's read-only with downloads blocked, and files can only be previewed in the web app. If she's using the desktop or mobile client, files may not open the way they did before. If Restricted Viewer was selected by mistake, switch her to Viewer.

3. Check her account status. Make sure her account isn't suspended or locked.

4. If you use SSO, check the group mapping. In Admin > SSO > Role Mapping, make sure her identity provider group maps to the role you intended. A mismatch can override a manual role change.

5. Have her sign out and back in. Ask her to sign out of CloudSync on every device and sign back in, then try opening a file in the web app. This clears out any outdated permissions on her session.

If she still can't open files, please send me the following so we can investigate:
- The exact error message or code she sees. If it's AUTH-002 (Permission Denied), that confirms the share or role is blocking access.
- Whether she's using the web app, desktop client, or mobile app.
- The name of the shared folder and her account email.
- Roughly when you changed her role.

If she needs to be back in the folder urgently, you can re-share it with her as a Viewer or Editor from the folder's Share menu. She can also use the "Request Access" button on the folder.

Please let me know what you find, and I'll gladly dig further into it.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

Hi there,

Thanks for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the confusion. Your situation is a common one. SYNC-001 (File Conflict) appears when two devices change the same file before CloudSync can sync them. That is what happened when one of you edited the budget spreadsheet offline during the flight while the other edited it online. CloudSync doesn't overwrite either version. It flags the conflict so you can decide how to handle it.

Here's how to resolve it while keeping both sets of changes:

1. **Close the spreadsheet on both computers.** This stops further edits or file locks from interfering while you resolve the conflict.
2. **Open the Conflict Resolver.** Go to Dashboard > Files > Conflicts and select the budget spreadsheet.
3. **Compare the two versions side by side.** Check the timestamps and file sizes. Ask each person to list the changes they made, such as which tabs, rows, or figures they edited, so you can tell which version holds which edits.
4. **Decide how to proceed:**
   - **If one version includes everything you need,** choose that version to keep.
   - **If both versions contain changes you need (the likely case here),** merge them manually. Open both versions, copy one person's changes into the other version, and check that the totals and formulas still look right. Then keep the merged file as the version you select.
5. **Click "Resolve"** to clear the conflict. Once it's cleared, the merged file will sync to both devices.

**Tip:** Before you click Resolve, save a separate copy of each version somewhere outside the synced folder, for example as "Budget_PersonA" and "Budget_PersonB". That way you have a backup of both sets of edits while you merge.

To avoid this in future, try to let CloudSync finish syncing before you start editing, especially after being offline. For files that more than one person edits, agree on who is editing at a given time.

If the Conflict Resolver doesn't show the file, or you can't tell which version has which changes, send me the file name, the approximate times each of you edited it, and a screenshot of what you see. I'll help you work through it.

Best regards,
CloudSync Support

Hi there,

Thank you for reaching out, and I'm sorry for the trouble. A client stuck on "Indexing" for two days, with folders that look empty, is frustrating. Your files are safe. They are still stored in CloudSync, which is why you can see them in the web dashboard.

What's happening: SYNC-004 (Index Corruption) means the local index the desktop client uses to track your files has become corrupted and can't be read. That explains both the stuck indexing and the empty folders on your computer. This usually happens after an unexpected shutdown during a sync, disk errors, or antivirus software interfering with the CloudSync data folder.

How to fix it:

1. Before you start, check that you have at least 500MB of free disk space and that you can reach the web dashboard.
2. In the desktop client, go to Settings > Sync > Reset Sync.
3. Confirm the reset. This clears only the local index and re-indexes your files from scratch. Nothing in your cloud storage is deleted.
4. Leave the client running while it re-indexes. This typically takes 10-30 minutes, depending on how many files you have.
5. When it finishes, check that the empty folders are populated again.

If the problem comes back or the reset doesn't work:

- Check your antivirus software and add the CloudSync data folder to its exclusions list. This stops it from interfering with the index.
- Uninstall and reinstall the desktop client. Your cloud files are not affected.

If SYNC-004 still appears after a reinstall, please reply with the following so we can investigate further:

- Your desktop client version (Settings > About)
- Your operating system
- Any recent unexpected shutdowns, power losses, or disk errors
- The recent log entries from Settings > Logs > View Recent
- Which folders appear empty, and whether they synced correctly before

CloudSync Support
